meaning.evidence: Every rule survives: "TDY travel is longer than 12 hours and needs a pre-approved authorisation in Concur.", "If you leave GSA, any unused travel comp time is lost."

sense.evidence: The plain swaps fit: "getting to and from work" for commuting, "runs out" for expires, "work out" for calculate.

authenticity.evidence: Reads as natural Australian workplace English: "Please get in touch with your Timekeeper", "Once you hit the expiry date, you lose the leave."

register.evidence: A shade under level 2: Australian spelling and plain phrasing ("Have a look", "check out") but almost no slang.

tone.evidence: Keeps the plain policy tone: "Travel comp time hours are based on elapsed time."

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "Travelling during your usual work day counts as regular hours, including getting to the airport from home."

variety.evidence: Little slang to vary; "work out" carries three of the calculations ("work out the breakdown", "For working out", "to work out elapsed time").

problems.why: Plain rewording with no Aussie colour; the text sits a little under the brief throughout.

problems.quote: Use the time zone where you departed from
problems.original: Use the time zone at departure
problems.why: 'Where you departed from' is a slightly clumsy double preposition.

A.summary: Plain, natural and faithful; a touch lighter than the brief.

meaning.evidence: The rules survive, but it invents examples of what counts as gap-filler time: "Think sitting at the gate, or stuck in a plane seat with your knees up round your ears." In a policy page that reads as guidance the original never gives. Other asides ("Sorry, the commute doesn't count.", "So use it or lose it.") restate the original.

sense.evidence: "Here's the go", "put in for", "Sing out", "tallying up" fit; "No fiddling with the clocks." implies a rule about cheating where the original only says which time zone to use.

authenticity.evidence: Natural idiom ("Here's the go:", "Sing out to your Timekeeper"), with stock tags bolted on: "That's what they're there for.", "simple as that", "Now, the catch."

register.evidence: Heavier than level 2: a yarn opener, a tag line after most paragraphs ("Everyone's in.", "No fiddling with the clocks."). No swearing.

tone.evidence: The plain policy tone turns chatty and jokey: "Sorry, the commute doesn't count.", "with your knees up round your ears".

flow.evidence: Reads easily, though the stream of tags breaks up the instructions.

variety.evidence: Varied: "Here's the go", "put in for", "trek", "squiz", "nitty-gritty", "Sing out", "tallying up", "use it or lose it".

essence.evidence: Still the policy page in shape, but recast as a friendly pep talk: "Now, the catch."

problems.quote: Think sitting at the gate, or stuck in a plane seat with your knees up round your ears.
problems.why: Invented examples of what qualifies, in a policy document.
Added aside implying a rule the original doesn't state.
Added quip; part of the over-weighting and tone shift.

B.summary: Lively and varied but over the brief, chatty in tone, with invented policy examples.

meaning.evidence: The original word for word, so every rule survives.

sense.evidence: No Aussie terms to misfire; only spellings change ("authorisation", "Travelling").

authenticity.evidence: No Australian voice at all, and US officialese left in: "When you reach the expiration date, you will forfeit the leave."

register.evidence: Untranslated apart from spelling; nowhere near a level 2 light touch.

variety.evidence: No slang at all to vary.

problems.quote: You may request travel comp time when you are approved to travel for work
problems.original: You may request travel comp time when you are approved to travel for work

C.summary: The original with spelling changes; fails the brief.

meaning.evidence: Every rule survives: "TDY travel runs more than 12 hours", "If you leave GSA, any unused travel comp time is forfeited."

sense.evidence: "There's no cap", "Have a squiz", "sing out to your Timekeeper" fit their contexts.

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian workplace English: "If you've got questions, sing out to your Timekeeper or an HR Specialist at your agency."

register.evidence: Light level 2 touch: "no cap", "squiz", "sing out", otherwise plain. No swearing.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "Travelling during your usual work day counts as regular hours, and that includes getting from home to the airport."

variety.evidence: Varied for its size: "no cap", "squiz", "sing out", "runs out"; "work out" recurs.

problems.original: Use the time zone at departure

D.summary: Light, natural and faithful; right on the brief.

meaning.evidence: Every rule survives, reordered without loss: "Anyone can earn travel comp time: there are no limits based on salary level or schedule type."

sense.evidence: "put in for", "have a squiz" fit; "Give your Timekeeper ... a shout" works, though in Australia "shout" also means buying a round.

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian workplace English: "If you're current GSA staff and want more detail".

register.evidence: Light level 2 touch: "put in for", "squiz", "a shout". No swearing.

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "The hours are based on elapsed time, and you work that out using the time zone you left from."

variety.evidence: Varied for its size: "put in for", "squiz", "a shout", "As a rule", "runs out".
